title: A morphism of short exact sequences lifts to a morphism between any two horseshoe resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. For a short exact sequence $S:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, call a *horseshoe resolution* of $S$ a datum $(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ of injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$, $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$, $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$ with $I_A^q=I_B^q=I_C^q=0$ for $q<0$ (so $0\to X\xrightarrow{s_X}I_X^0\to I_X^1\to\cdots$ is exact for $X=A,B,C$) and morphisms of complexes $\alpha:I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet$, $\beta:I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet$ with $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$ and $0\to I_A^n\xrightarrow{\alpha^n}I_B^n\xrightarrow{\beta^n}I_C^n\to0$ short exact for every $n\ge0$. Let $S':0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be a second short exact sequence, $(a,b,c)$ a morphism from $S$ to $S'$ (morphisms $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $c:C\to C'$ with $bf=f'a$, $cg=g'b$), $(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ a horseshoe resolution of $S$ and $(s'_{A'},s'_{B'},s'_{C'},\alpha',\beta')$ a horseshoe resolution of $S'$, with complexes $I_{A'}'^\bullet,I_{B'}'^\bullet,I_{C'}'^\bullet$. Let $\varphi_A:I_A^\bullet\to I_{A'}'^\bullet$ and $\varphi_C:I_C^\bullet\to I_{C'}'^\bullet$ be any morphisms of complexes with $\varphi_A^0s_A=s'_{A'}a$ and $\varphi_C^0s_C=s'_{C'}c$ (such morphisms exist by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]). Then there is a morphism of complexes $\varphi_B:I_B^\bullet\to I_{B'}'^\bullet$ with $\varphi_B^0s_B=s'_{B'}b$, $\varphi_B\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ\varphi_A$ and $\beta'\circ\varphi_B=\varphi_C\circ\beta$; that is, $(\varphi_A,\varphi_B,\varphi_C)$ is a morphism of short exact sequences of complexes lifting $(a,b,c)$.

source.place: No Stacks statement. Classical: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, proof of Theorem 2.4.6 (naturality of the connecting maps; dual of the horseshoe Lemma 2.2.8), not in literature/ (WANTED). Stacks ingredients for a proof: homology.tex Lemma Tag 0136 (lemma-characterize-injectives: a short exact sequence starting with an injective splits), derived.tex Lemma Tag 013R (lemma-acyclic-is-zero: a morphism from an acyclic complex to a bounded below complex of injectives is homotopic to zero), derived.tex Lemma Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift, for the existence of phi_A, phi_C). Route found by the worker of lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor (checked by hand, signs included): choose degreewise splittings r, sigma of the rows of the first horseshoe and r', sigma' of the second (0136); chi := alpha' phi_A r + sigma' phi_C beta satisfies chi alpha = alpha' phi_A and beta' chi = phi_C beta; D := d chi - chi d satisfies D alpha = 0 and beta' D = 0, so D^n = alpha' E^n beta for unique E^n: I_C^n -> I'_A^{n+1}, and chi^0 s_B - s'_B b = alpha' e g for a unique e: C -> I'_A^0; then dE + Ed = 0 and E^0 s_C = d e, so u^{-1} = e, u^n = (-1)^n E^n is a morphism from the acyclic augmented complex C -> I_C^0 -> I_C^1 -> ... (C in degree -1) to the complex of injectives with m-th term I'_A^{m+1}; by 013R it is null-homotopic by h^m (h^{-1} = 0); with k^n = (-1)^n h^n one has E^n = d k^n - k^{n+1} d and e = k^0 s_C, and phi_B := chi - alpha' k beta works.
